title: The Woman Who Was Already Cremated — Episode 5

characters.persona: Returned mother whose identity has been officially buried
Police sub-inspector assigned to verify Meera’s identity
Meera’s father who identified the burned body
Meera’s younger son who wants his mother restored immediately
Meera’s teenage daughter who remembers a private detail only her mother should k

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: This door. Break this door, and I will show you where they kept me.
lines.sfx_cue: metal latch rattling, fists striking wooden door
lines.spoken: This door. Break this door, and I will show you where they kept me.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Nobody breaks my property. Show me a warrant or leave my courtyard.
lines.spoken: Nobody breaks my property. Show me a warrant, or leave my courtyard.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Open the room. Refuse again, and I will seal the entire floor until a magistrate decides who enters it.
lines.spoken: Open the room. Refuse again, and I will seal the entire floor until a magistrate decides who enters it.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: You police people arrive after eighteen months and speak as though dust committed the crime.
lines.spoken: You police people arrive after eighteen months and speak as though dust committed the crime.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: I slept behind that door. I counted the cracks above the window every night.
lines.spoken: I slept behind that door. I counted the cracks above the window… every night.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I have never rented a room to any Meera.
lines.spoken: I have never rented a room to any Meera.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Then we have travelled to Kota for another false memory.
lines.spoken: Then we have travelled to Kota for another false memory.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: She knew the staircase without anyone showing her.
lines.spoken: She knew the staircase without anyone showing her.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: That does not mean she lived here.
lines.spoken: That does not mean she lived here.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: There are seventeen steps. The sixth one is broken at the edge. The room has a green wall and no fan regulator.
lines.spoken: There are seventeen steps. The sixth one is broken at the edge. The room has a green wall… and no fan regulator.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Every room upstairs has a green wall.
lines.spoken: Every room upstairs has a green wall.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: And the broken sixth step?
lines.spoken: And the broken sixth step?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: People notice stairs while climbing them.
lines.spoken: People notice stairs while climbing them.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: There is a water stain shaped like a hook beside the window.
lines.spoken: There is a water stain shaped like a hook, beside the window.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Enough. The room was rented to another woman.
lines.spoken: Enough. The room was rented to another woman.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Name.
lines.spoken: Name.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Sarla.
lines.spoken: Sarla.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: That is what Shahid called me in front of strangers.
lines.spoken: That is what Shahid called me… in front of strangers.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I do not know any Shahid.
lines.spoken: I do not know any Shahid.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: You answered before I asked whether you knew him.
lines.spoken: You answered before I asked whether you knew him.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Because she has repeated the name three times in my courtyard.
lines.spoken: Because she has repeated the name three times in my courtyard.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Madam, open the room. Either her details are correct, or we end this journey here.
lines.spoken: Madam, open the room. Either her details are correct, or we end this journey here.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You are waiting for me to fail.
lines.spoken: You are waiting for me to fail.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I am waiting for evidence that does not change whenever a new person arrives.
lines.spoken: I am waiting for evidence that does not change whenever a new person arrives.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: If she is wrong about one stain, will you take her away?
lines.spoken: If she is wrong about one stain… will you take her away?

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: No. One room does not decide her identity.
lines.spoken: No. One room does not decide her identity.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Good. Then decide it somewhere else.
lines.spoken: Good. Then decide it somewhere else.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Constable, call the local station and request a property seal.
lines.spoken: Constable, call the local station and request a property seal.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Wait. There is no need to spoil everyone's day over one empty room.
lines.spoken: Wait. There is no need to spoil everyone's day over one empty room.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: It was not empty when you collected rent.
lines.spoken: It was not empty when you collected rent.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I collected rent from Sarla's guardian.
lines.spoken: I collected rent from Sarla's guardian.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Guardian? She was an adult tenant.
lines.spoken: Guardian? She was an adult tenant.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: That was the word he used.
lines.spoken: That was the word he used.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Who was he?
lines.spoken: Who was he?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: A transport man. I do not remember every customer.
lines.spoken: A transport man. I do not remember every customer.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You remember enough to change the word landlord into guardian.
lines.spoken: You remember enough to change the word landlord… into guardian.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: I remember rent paid on time. That is all.
lines.spoken: I remember rent paid on time. That is all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lock opened. Meera stepped inside before anyone invited her.
lines.spoken: The lock opened. Meera stepped inside before anyone invited her.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: The cot was against this wall.
lines.spoken: The cot was against this wall.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: It is against the other wall now.
lines.spoken: It is against the other wall now.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Move it. Please. There should be writing behind the headboard.
lines.spoken: Move it. Please. There should be writing behind the headboard.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: There is no writing. I repaint between tenants.
lines.spoken: There is no writing. I repaint between tenants.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You did not repaint behind the cot.
lines.spoken: You did not repaint behind the cot.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Constable, move it carefully.
lines.spoken: Constable, move it carefully.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: There are lines on the wall.
lines.spoken: There are lines on the wall.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Thirty-four vertical marks. Some crossed in groups of seven.
lines.spoken: Thirty-four vertical marks. Some crossed in groups of seven.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: I marked the nights when he took the outside bolt off.
lines.spoken: I marked the nights when he took the outside bolt off.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Anyone could make marks.
lines.spoken: Anyone could make marks.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: The last group stops halfway because Shahid came early.
lines.spoken: The last group stops halfway… because Shahid came early.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: She is inventing meaning for scratches.
lines.spoken: She is inventing meaning for scratches.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Then tell me why this bedroom door has an outside bolt.
lines.spoken: Then tell me why this bedroom door has an outside bolt.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: For luggage security.
lines.spoken: For luggage security.

lines.speaker: VOICE FROM COURTYARD
lines.text: Luggage does not sleep in the room and cry at night.
lines.spoken: Luggage does not sleep in the room… and cry at night.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Who said that? Come upstairs and give your name.
lines.spoken: Who said that? Come upstairs and give your name.

lines.speaker: SECOND VOICE FROM COURTYARD
lines.text: We all heard someone. None of us wants our name in your ledger.
lines.spoken: We all heard someone. None of us wants our name in your ledger.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: They heard me.
lines.spoken: They heard me.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: They heard a person. I will take individual statements before deciding more.
lines.spoken: They heard a person. I will take individual statements before deciding more.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Look above the window. The hook-shaped stain.
lines.spoken: Look above the window. The hook-shaped stain.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: It is there.
lines.spoken: It is there.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Stains survive tenants. It could be older than her claim.
lines.spoken: Stains survive tenants. It could be older than her claim.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: Why do you make every correct answer smaller?
lines.spoken: Why do you make every correct answer smaller?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Because you are a child, and somebody must protect you from wanting too much.
lines.spoken: Because you are a child, and somebody must protect you from wanting too much.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: I only want Ma.
lines.spoken: I only want Ma.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: You want this woman to be Ma.
lines.spoken: You want this woman to be Ma.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: She knows things Ma knew.
lines.spoken: She knows things Ma knew.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Things can be told.
lines.spoken: Things can be told.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Tara is right to be afraid.
lines.spoken: Tara is right… to be afraid.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Do not tell me what I feel.
lines.spoken: Do not tell me what I feel.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Then I won't.
lines.spoken: Then I won't.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Meera, what else should be in this room? Something removable, not a wall or stain.
lines.spoken: Meera, what else should be in this room? Something removable, not a wall or stain.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: A brass button under the window ledge. I pushed it into a crack.
lines.spoken: A brass button under the window ledge. I pushed it into a crack.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Now we will search for buttons in an old building?
lines.spoken: Now we will search for buttons in an old building?

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Yes. Evidence is often smaller than the person hiding it.
lines.spoken: Yes. Evidence is often smaller than the person hiding it.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Why a brass button?
lines.spoken: Why a brass button?

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: It came off Mohan's brown sweater. I found it in my blouse pocket after they brought me here.
lines.spoken: It came off Mohan's brown sweater. I found it in my blouse pocket… after they brought me here.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: The sweater with the bear?
lines.spoken: The sweater with the bear?

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: No. The one you hated. Brown wool, wooden train stitched near the collar.
lines.spoken: No. The one you hated. Brown wool, wooden train stitched near the collar.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: It scratched my neck.
lines.spoken: It scratched my neck.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You cried whenever I pulled it over your ears.
lines.spoken: You cried whenever I pulled it over your ears.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: What did you sing?
lines.spoken: What did you sing?

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Mohan, not here.
lines.spoken: Mohan… not here.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: What did you sing when I would not put my head through?
lines.spoken: What did you sing when I would not put my head through?

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Little train, little train, wait beside the door. Mohan has one stubborn head, but Ma has counted four.
lines.spoken: Little train, little train… wait beside the door. Mohan has one stubborn head, but Ma has counted four.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: No. You missed the next part.
lines.spoken: No. You missed the next part.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: I don't... I thought you had forgotten it.
lines.spoken: I don't… I thought you had forgotten it.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: Sing it properly.
lines.spoken: Sing it properly.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: One for anger, one for tears, one that asks for sweets. The fourth comes out when morning starts, and kisses both my cheeks.
lines.spoken: One for anger, one for tears, one that asks for sweets. The fourth comes out when morning starts… and kisses both my cheeks.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: Ma.
lines.spoken: Ma…

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Mohan—
lines.spoken: Mohan—

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: She is my Ma. I am saying it where everybody can hear me. She is my Ma.
lines.spoken: She is my Ma! I am saying it where everybody can hear me. She is my Ma.

lines.speaker: VOICE FROM COURTYARD
lines.text: The boy has recognised his mother.
lines.spoken: The boy has recognised his mother.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: A lullaby proves memory, not identity.
lines.spoken: A lullaby proves memory, not identity.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: Then my memory is better than yours.
lines.spoken: Then my memory is better than yours.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: I found the crack beneath the ledge.
lines.spoken: I found the crack beneath the ledge.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: There is no button. But the plaster has been disturbed recently.
lines.spoken: There is no button. But the plaster has been disturbed recently.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Repairs happen. You cannot arrest a wall.
lines.spoken: Repairs happen. You cannot arrest a wall.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Where is the rental ledger?
lines.spoken: Where is the rental ledger?

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: You have seen the room. Leave my records alone.
lines.spoken: You have seen the room. Leave my records alone.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The room was rented under another name. The ledger is now part of the verification.
lines.spoken: The room was rented under another name. The ledger is now part of the verification.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Old books are downstairs. Some pages may be damaged.
lines.spoken: Old books are downstairs. Some pages may be damaged.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: If one page is missing, the entire ledger goes into evidence.
lines.spoken: If one page is missing, the entire ledger goes into evidence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Downstairs, the landlord opened a steel trunk and lifted out a red cloth book.
lines.sfx_cue: steel trunk lid opening, paper rustling
lines.spoken: Downstairs, the landlord opened a steel trunk… and lifted out a red cloth book.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Here. Sarla. Room twelve. Rent paid in cash.
lines.spoken: Here. Sarla. Room twelve. Rent paid in cash.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The tenant column contains a different name, but this signature does not say Sarla.
lines.spoken: The tenant column contains a different name… but this signature does not say Sarla.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: That is my name.
lines.spoken: That is my name.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: No. No, that date cannot be right.
lines.spoken: No. No, that date cannot be right.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Read it aloud.
lines.spoken: Read it aloud.

lines.speaker: LANDLORD
lines.text: Twenty-first of June, twenty twenty-one.
lines.spoken: Twenty-first of June… twenty twenty-one.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: By then, our family believed Meera had already been cremated.
lines.spoken: By then, our family believed Meera had already been cremated.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: And beside that date, the rental ledger contains Meera's signature.
lines.spoken: And beside that date… the rental ledger contains Meera's signature.
